findings.our_note: Devil: شيط 70 + شياطين 18 = 88 confirmed (the plural needs the شياط pattern because the dagger alif breaks the شيط substring). Angels: ملائكة 73 confirmed; singular malak-as-angel is about 11-12 by verse inspection (6:8, 6:9, 6:50, 11:12, 11:31, 12:31, 25:7, 32:11, 53:26, 69:17, 89:22, plus dual الملكين 2:102), giving a total of about 85 — three short of 88. source.author: Harun Yahya (Adnan Oktar)
source.title: Miracles of the Qur'an (Goodword Books, 2005) — 'Word Repetitions in the Qur'an'

findings.claim: The word 'day' (yawm) occurs 365 times, matching the days of a (Gregorian) year.
findings.corpus_and_method: Method not stated by the source; our recount reproduces 365 only under a stated selective method (see note).
findings.our_note: Simple forms يوم/اليوم/يوما = 274; plus prefixed ويوم 44, واليوم 23, ليوم 8, فاليوم 8, بيوم 5, باليوم 2, وباليوم 1 = 365 exactly. Caveat: suffixed forms (يومكم, يومهم, يومئذ 65+), dual يومين and plural أيام are excluded by this method; all tokens containing يوم = 590, polluted by belief verbs (يؤمنون). The Islamic calendar has 354/355 days, so the Gregorian-365 framing is itself a critique point (WikiIslam).

findings.our_note: Man singular (رجل family): رجل 13 + رجلا 7 + لرجل 2 + فرجل 1 + ورجلا 1 = 24. Woman singular (امرأة family): امرات 6 + امراتهي 5 + امراة 3 + وامراتهي 2 + امراتك 2 + امراتى 2 + وامراتى 1 + لامراتهو 1 + وامراة 1 + وامرات 1 = 24. Harun Yahya's own list gives 23/23 — one short on each side. With duals/plurals: man 30 (excl. feet), woman 26. Naive substrings both give 45/45 only by coincidence (رجل mixes in 13-15 foot/feet forms; امرا mixes in امرأ 'man' 19 and السامري 1).

findings.claim: The total number of verses in the Quran is 6,346 = 19 x 334 (6,234 numbered verses + 112 unnumbered Basmalahs).
findings.corpus_and_method: Standard Hafs count is 6,236 verses; Khalifa's figure rests on counting basmalahs as verses and deleting 9:128-129.
findings.our_note: The arithmetic checks out (6,236 + 112 - 2 = 6,346) but the deletion of 9:128-129 is the contested step: with those verses the Allah count would be 2,699 not 2,698 and Rahim 115 not 114. The scholarly consensus rejects the deletion (see the reception finding).

findings.claim: Khalifa's 19-based 'mathematical miracle' was published from 1973-1989 and drew both praise and sustained scholarly/skeptical criticism.
findings.corpus_and_method: Literature review (bibliographic sources, verified by web search 2026-11-06).
findings.our_note: Timeline: initials research from 1969; Miracle of the Quran: Significance of the Mysterious Alphabets (1973); the 19-code claimed January 1974; The Computer Speaks: God's Message to the World (1981); Quran: Visual Presentation of the Miracle (1982); Quran: The Final Testament translation (1989). Reception: Martin Gardner, Scientific American, September 1980, p. 22 ('ingenious study...'); critical review in Skeptical Inquirer 21(5), September-October 1997, pp. 16-17, 58; Canadian Council on the Study of Religion, Quarterly Review, April 1983 (quoted by proponents as calling it 'an authenticating proof'); Bilal Philips, The Qur'an's Numerical Miracle: Hoax and Heresy (1987); Ziauddin Sardar, Explorations in Islamic Science (1989) on the Nun spelling and letter-count selectivity; Edip Yüksel (proponent), Nineteen: God's Signature in Nature and Scripture (Brainbow Press, 2011); Abdullah Arik, Beyond Probability (2012); Matthew Stanley, A Miracle on Trial (2016). Submission.org's own 2002 recount confirmed Khalifa's initial counts 'except for a few counts' (submission.org/App1.html).

findings.claim: Root-frequency studies of the Quran (QAC 0.4) find about 1,650 roots; the most frequent root is Alh (Allah), about 2,851 occurrences.
findings.corpus_and_method: Corpus-based root counts from QAC 0.4 morphology (abdulbaqi.io 2019; thequran.love 2026; Malkoç 2025). Root counting is the sibling agents' task; not recounted here.
findings.our_note: abdulbaqi.io (2019): 1,651 roots; top roots Alh 2,851, qwl 1,722, kwn 1,390, rbb 980 (data file quranic-corpus-morphology-0.4.txt, 128,276 lines). Zia H Shah / thequran.love (2026): 1,642 roots, verbal-only counts (qwl 1,618, kwn 1,358), 49,967 root-bearing tokens (64.5%). Muzaffer Malkoç, Beauty as Method (Zenodo, 2025): root concordance via Tanzil + Abd al-Baqi's al-Mu'jam al-Mufahras, e.g. Ḥ-S-N 194. findings.claim: Classical authorities give the Quran's word total as 77,439 (with variants 77,430 / 77,437 / 77,797 / 77,934).
findings.corpus_and_method: Classical counts (al-Suyuti, al-Itqan; Basra reciters; Ata' bin Yasar); our recount on the Tanzil file.
findings.our_note: Our 77,433 (excl. unnumbered basmalahs) is 6 below the lowest classical figure (77,439) — within the spread of counting conventions. Kufan reciters recorded 77,430, Basran 77,437 (arabiantongue.com).

findings.claim: Classical authorities give the Quran's letter total as 323,671 (with variants 323,015 / 330,733).
findings.corpus_and_method: Classical counts (al-Suyuti via Yahya ibn al-Harith and others); our recount on the Tanzil file under a stated convention (see meta).
findings.our_note: Our 325,386 (excl. unnumbered basmalahs) matches none of the classical figures exactly; the classical sources disagree among themselves by up to 7,718 (323,015 vs 330,733), and further variants exist (Mujahid 321,000; Ibn Mas'ud 300,670; Salam Abu Muhammad 340,740), so no single letter total is settled. The variation is partly definitional (e.g. whether a doubled letter counts as one or two).

meta.corpus: Tanzil Quran Text, Uthmani script (corpus/quran-uthmani.txt), 6,236 verses, downloaded 2026-11-06 from tanzil.net
meta.project: miracleMath — scholar findings on the Quran corpus
meta.recount_method: Whitespace tokens. Skeleton normalisation for matching: diacritics/tatweel removed; hamza variants normalised (أ إ آ ٱ → ا, ؤ → و, ئ → ي, ء dropped); dagger alif ٰ → ا, small waw ۥ → و, small yeh ۦ → ي are kept as letters for matching. Letter-counting convention: base letters count, including alef wasla ٱ as ا; dagger alif, small waw and small yeh are marks and do NOT count; standalone hamza ء counts. This convention reproduces the anchors: basmalah = 19 letters, 96:1-5 = 76 letters, 110:1 = 19 letters. 'Excl. unnumbered basmalahs' means excluding the 112 basmalahs merged into verse 1 of surahs 2-8 and 10-114 (the 2 numbered basmalahs, 1:1 and 27:30, are kept). Surah boundaries use the standard Hafs verse-count table (sums to 6,236).
meta.warning: Disputed numerology is presented here as reported findings with a source and a status — never as settled fact. our_status 'confirmed' means our own scripted recount on the Tanzil file reproduces the claimed figure under a stated method; 'differs' means it does not; 'cannot_verify' means no recount was possible or the claim needs sense disambiguation.
